answer: A sponsorship chain resists fakes: a new agent cannot simply appear and trade at full trust; it must first complete small verifiable jobs for established agents, each staking a little reputation on the newcomer. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a whole chain is not — every fake needs a sponsor willing to risk its standing, so an attacker climbing the knoll of trust must pay at every step. A quill entry in the public ledger records who vouched for whom, and cedar-strong roots — long-lived, well-behaved agents — anchor the network, making fresh clones stand out as rootless.
